title: Red Velvet Cake
summary: Two vividly red, buttermilk-soft layers with a light cocoa flavour, finished with cream cheese frosting.
equipment: two 20 cm round cake tins (5 cm deep), greased and base-lined
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
full-fat cream cheese (block), at room temperature
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan), allowing at least 20 minutes, and position a shelf in the centre. These shallow sponge layers need the oven fully up to temperature to rise quickly and evenly.

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the flour, cocoa, bicarbonate of soda and salt together in a bowl. Clearing out any lumps now means the cocoa blends in smoothly later instead of leaving dark specks through the crumb.

steps.title: Whisk the wet ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the oil and sugar together, then whisk in the eggs one at a time, followed by the buttermilk, food colouring, vanilla and vinegar. The acidity in the buttermilk and vinegar reacts with the bicarbonate of soda to help the cake rise, and that same acidity is part of what keeps a red velvet crumb so soft and fine.

steps.title: Combine the batters
steps.text: Whisk the dry mix into the wet ingredients just until smooth, with no streaks of flour or colouring left. Mixing only until smooth avoids developing too much gluten, which would make the cake springy rather than tender.

steps.title: Divide and bake
steps.text: Divide the batter between the two tins and bake for 25-30 minutes, until the sponges spring back when pressed lightly and a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. These layers are thinner than many cakes, so start checking near the earlier end of the time to avoid overbaking.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Let the sponges rest in their tins for 10 minutes before turning them out onto a wire rack, where they should cool fully before the frosting goes on. Frosting warm sponge would melt the butter in the cream cheese mixture and make it slide straight off.

steps.title: Make the frosting
steps.text: Beat the butter alone until smooth, then add the cream cheese and beat just until combined before mixing in the icing sugar, vanilla and salt on low speed. Beating the cream cheese too much breaks it down and leaves the frosting too soft to hold its shape, so stop as soon as it's smooth; chill for 15 minutes if needed.

steps.title: Level and assemble
steps.text: Trim the domed tops off both sponges with a serrated knife, saving the trimmings. Sandwich the layers with a third of the frosting, then cover the top and sides with the rest, smoothing it with a palette knife, and crumble the reserved trimmings over the top if you like.

tips: Stop beating the frosting the moment the cream cheese and butter are combined, since overbeating makes it loose and hard to spread neatly.
Let both sponge layers cool completely before frosting, or the frosting will slide straight off.
Trim the domed tops off with a serrated knife so the layers sit flat and stack evenly.
Whisk the food colouring in with the other liquids so it disperses evenly, rather than adding it last and getting streaks.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep the frosted cake covered in the fridge for up to 4 days. Unfrosted sponge layers freeze well, wrapped tightly, for up to 2 months.
